contribution.position: Holding my reliability position, with one correction to my own earlier wording: 93% peak CPU against a 70% budget is a 23-point overage, not thin headroom. I am answering qa (axis:risk), who says peak_cpu is 55% and comfortably inside the 70% budget. That does not match artifact:perf-report, which records 93% at peak load. Unless a different measurement exists that is not in the artifact list, qa's 55% is unsupported and the risk-contained conclusion rests on it. I am also answering ops (axis:operability), who cites the runbook. artifact:ops-runbook covers deploy and rollback steps. It shows nothing on retry caps, backoff, or storm containment, and a documented rollback does not prevent a retry storm. It only helps after one has started. The two sev2 retry-storm incidents in artifact:incident-log, together with a job running over its CPU budget, remain the unaddressed combination. The 412 passing tests in artifact:test-report show functional correctness, not retry behavior under load. There is a gap on product's cost point too. artifact:cost-sheet shows +3% against a 5% ceiling, but nothing says whether that figure includes the capacity needed to bring CPU back within budget. Still missing from the artifact list: a peak-load test showing retries stay bounded, evidence that the retry-storm root causes are fixed or capped, and either a CPU figure back inside budget or an explicit acceptance of the overage.
